description: This bar chart, titled “Average number of tokens under different numbers of shots with few-shot style,” illustrates the average token count for two categories—“Reasoning” (represented by orange bars) and “Demonstration” (represented by blue bars)—across five different “Number of Shots” conditions, labeled 0 through 4 on the horizontal axis. The vertical axis, labeled “Token Count,” is scaled linearly from 0 to 7000, with major gridlines and tick marks at intervals of 1000. The chart employs a stacked bar format, where the orange segment represents the “Reasoning” token count and the blue segment on top represents the “Demonstration” token count. For the “0” shots condition, the orange bar reaches a value of 6393, with no blue segment shown. For the “1” shots condition, the orange bar reaches 4348 (implied by the -1952 annotation above it), topped by a blue segment of 1952, totaling 6300. For “2” shots, the orange bar reaches 4713 (implied by the -1613 annotation), topped by a blue segment of 1613, totaling 6326. For “3” shots, the orange bar reaches 5000 (implied by the -1040 annotation), topped by a blue segment of 1040, totaling 6040. For “4” shots, the orange bar reaches 4400 (implied by the -1379 annotation), topped by a blue segment of 1379, totaling 5779. Each bar is annotated with a red arrow pointing to its top, displaying the numerical value of the blue segment, which is consistently negative, indicating a reduction in token count relative to the previous condition. The bars are sorted in ascending order of “Number of Shots,” from left to right. The chart does not visually emphasize any bars beyond the color-coding and annotations.
